Dear Fellow Shareholder,
A vintage year for Arotech
2013 was in all respects our best year ever. Revenues reached $89 million, we reported EBITDA
of $6.5 million, and, most importantly, we showed a GAAP net profit of $2.3 million – all of which were
records for our company. Both our Simulation Division and our Battery Division reached record revenues and profits, with our Battery Division showing EBITDA of almost $1.5 million and our Simulation
Division showing EBITDA of over $10 million.
We also successfully completed an underwritten public offering in September, which raised
$6,900,000. These proceeds were critical in allowing us this past April to successfully acquire UEC
Electronics, a specialist in electronic subsystem for military and commercial applications. The year also demonstrated the success of our strategy of focusing on our existing battery and power systems
and simulation businesses. We are bidding on programs in both divisions that we are confident will allow us to continue to grow our company.
Finally, in 2013 we launched a major new program to develop an energy storage battery. The
worldwide market for storage batteries is projected to grow to $400 billion by 2030, which makes it a
huge market opportunity. While there will be several competitive technologies, we believe that our iron
flow storage battery will have cost and operational advantages, which should allow us to achieve a
significant participation in this emerging market. We hope to have a working lab model within a year
and, if it is successful, move ahead with a large scale prototype in 2015-16. We are optimistic about
the growth in our core businesses during the near term, and hope that the longer term will see us a
major player in the larger energy storage business as well.

the larger energy storage business as well.
One last word. This will be my last letter to you as Chief Executive Officer of Arotech. While I will
continue as Executive Chairman, on October first of this year Steven Esses, who has been associated with Arotech since 2002 and has been Arotech’s President since 2006, will take over the role of
CEO. Steven is well prepared for this additional responsibility, both by his deep business experience
prior to joining Arotech and through our having worked together for the last twelve years, during which
time I have been grooming him for this new challenge.
I am pleased to be able to assure you that Steven is more than prepared and qualified to take
over this important role. He has the sound judgment and dedication to take Arotech to the next level
of growth, and I know you join me in wishing him well and success upon his becoming the CEO of
Arotech.
Sincerely,
Robert S. Ehrlich
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer

Electronics, LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company that develops and manufactures electronic components and subsystems primarily for military, aerospace and industrial customers. smart power subsystems for military vehicles and dismounted applications, and aircraft and missile systems support for cutting-edge weapons and communications technologies. The following annual report does not reflect our
acquisition of UEC or our integration of UEC’s business lines into our Battery and Power Systems Division.
